newsitem.title: VATICAN: Vatican denies report Pope may have new tumour.
newsitem.headline: Vatican denies report Pope may have new tumour.

text.p: The Vatican denied on Thursday an Italian news agency report that Pope John Paul may be suffering from a new tumour.
The 76-year-old Pope, who goes into the hospital on Sunday to remove his appendix, had a colon tumour removed in a 1992 operation.
The small news agency ASCA reported on Thursday that doctors had not excluded the possibility that a new tumour has been the cause of the Pope's recent illnesses and discomfort.
Chief Vatican spokesman Joaquin Navarro-Valls said medical statements about the Polish Pope released by the Vatican in August and September were still valid.
Those statements said tests had shown that there had been no recurrence of the 1992 tumour.
ASCA, which specialises in Italian politics and religious affairs, said "reliable" medical sources had told its reporters that a new tumour could not be excluded.
The report said a CAT scan, the type of test the Pope had in August, did not always detect intestinal tumours and asserted that the Pope had refused to undergo endoscopic tests.
In these, a tube with a light at the end and an optical system is inserted into the intestine either via the mouth or colon.
The Vatican and the Pope's personal doctor, Renato Buzzonetti, have said the Pope is suffering from a recurring inflamed appendix which has caused several fevers and pain in the past nine months.

Some doctors in Italy and abroad who are not treating the Pope have expressed scepticism about the Vatican's official version of what is ailing the leader of the world's some 960 million Roman Catholics.
The Pontiff is due to underdo surgery to remove the appendix at Rome's Gemelli hospital either on Monday or Tuesday.
